sections_inspected: From the opening discussion of zoon logon echon and homo faber through “The meaning of technique,” “The western conception of technique,” “Technique, creation and the constitution of the human world,” “The neutrality of technique,” “Technique and social organisation,” and “Technique and politics”
scope_outcomes.criterion: A relevant instance requires an explicit definition, distinction, redefinition, or materially different local use of a concept in the supplied text, with its object and boundary preserved.
scope_outcomes.basis: The source explicitly distinguishes Greek techne from contemporary technique, defines technique as absolute creation and as a constitutive social dimension, qualifies its neutrality, and rejects strict technical determination of social organisation.
limitations: The assessment concerns the supplied source text only.
Some quoted formulations are discussed through cited figures and traditions, but the findings report how the text presents those formulations rather than independently verifying the cited works.
